## Overview

Add expert LoRA to the fused FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE kernel for NVFP4 (W4A4) experts with per-token activation scales (`TrtLlmNvFp4LoRAExperts`). This is the NVFP4 sibling of #61979 (MXFP4) and reuses the same `_TrtLlmLoRAExpertsBase` flow and the same routed FlashInfer API (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` with `gemm1_lora_delta`).

## Claims

- NVFP4 MoE models with per-token FC1 activation scales (`kNvfp4DynamicToken`: ModelOpt `moe.activation='nvfp4_per_token'`, or online `nvfp4_per_token` quantization) can serve expert LoRA adapters on `moe_backend="flashinfer_trtllm"`. On main this raises `kernel does not support LoRA`.
- Opt-in: `moe_backend="auto"` selects the same backend as before (Marlin when LoRA is enabled). NVFP4 with static input scales plus expert LoRA is rejected with an explicit reason (`kernel does not support quantization scheme ...`), because the kernel then returns the FC1 activation as packed FP4 without its block scales (see Details).
- The non-LoRA `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsModular` is unchanged in behavior: its kernel arguments move into `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsBase._routed_moe_kwargs`, which both classes use.

## Validation

Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly arm64 image built from `8e2beaa3b` (flashinfer-python 0.7.2, torch 2.14.0+cu130), NVIDIA GB300 and GB200. The changed files of this PR were applied onto that commit's copies (cleanly) and copied over the image; tests ran from `tests/` at that commit plus the new test file. Not run on the PR base itself; the three changed files at `8e2beaa3b` match the PR base except one unrelated line.

**Kernel-level**, `pytest tests/lora/test_trtllm_nvfp4_lora_moe.py -v`:

- without this PR: collection error (`TrtLlmNvFp4LoRAExperts` does not exist), 0 passed;
- with this PR: 28 passed.

Random NVFP4 weights go through vLLM's TRTLLM conversion (`convert_to_nvfp4_moe_kernel_format`, `make_nvfp4_moe_quant_config`, `process_weights_after_loading`). The reference is float64 from the dequantized weights, with the FC1 and FC2 inputs quantized per token as the kernel does.

- Delta in `[up | gate]` order: FC1 activation 0.19% and output 2.1% relative error vs. the reference (bounds 2% / 5%); the swapped order is 66% off; the delta itself moves the reference by 59%.
- Zero delta vs. the non-LoRA path: bitwise equal in this run (the test asserts < 2%); the non-LoRA path is 0.23% off the reference.
- Delta layout: per-expert and fused 3D adapters are converted exactly.
- Full `apply` with real punica metadata against a float64 reference (base and LoRA added separately): rank 8/16/64, one adapter, mixed LoRA/no-LoRA batch, 4 adapters, no-LoRA batch (bitwise equal to the base path), SwiGLU clamp, EP2 (`expert_map` + local expert offset), batches above 192 tokens per local expert, the same under FlashInfer autotuning, and batches above the launch limit. CUDA graph replay is bitwise equal to eager. Flipping the w13 slices, dropping the w2 delta, ignoring `expert_map` or dropping the clamp each fails the corresponding cases.
- Oracle: with LoRA and an explicit `flashinfer_trtllm`, per-token selects `TrtLlmNvFp4LoRAExperts` for Renormalize, RenormalizeNaive, DeepSeekV3, Sigmoid and EP2. Static scales raise naming the quantization scheme, and Llama4 routing raises naming the routing method. `auto` with LoRA does not select TRTLLM, and without LoRA the selection is unchanged.

Oracle selection measured on the same GPU, before and after:

| `moe_backend` | LoRA | activation scales | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | no | static / per-token | TRTLLM `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsModular` | same |
| `auto` | yes | static | `MarlinExperts` | same |
| `auto` | yes | per-token | `MarlinExperts`, then ModelOpt rejects it (per-token needs TRTLLM) | same |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | no | static / per-token | TRTLLM `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsModular` | same |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | yes | static | error: no LoRA support | error: quantization scheme |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | yes | per-token | error: no LoRA support | `TrtLlmNvFp4LoRAExperts` |

Non-LoRA path: `test_trtllm_fp4_moe_no_graph` now asserts the full kwarg set passed to `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` matches the previous explicit call (23 passed, 2 skipped on both main and this PR; dropping one kwarg fails 19 cases). GSM8K, `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy (GB200):

| config | experts class | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP2 + EP | `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsModular` | 0.871 / 0.884 (two runs) | 0.877 |
| TP1 | `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsMonolithic` | 0.882 | 0.884 |

**End-to-end** (GB200): `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` with per-token MoE activations plus `jeeejeee/qwen3-moe-text2sql-spider` (rank 8), `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm`, default `max_num_batched_tokens`. Reference: the same model on Marlin with the same adapter.

- Teacher-forced LoRA logprobs: mean |Δ| vs. Marlin 0.042; two runs of this PR differ by 0.036. The adapter moves logprobs by ~7.8 on both backends. The 4 reference text2sql questions are exact matches on both.
- In a mixed batch, no-LoRA requests are identical to the same requests run alone.
- Decode output tok/s (256 tokens, CUDA graphs): LoRA bs 1/8/64: 139 / 954 / 4544 (Marlin LoRA at a 384-token budget: 150 / 1024 / 3051); no-LoRA: 315 / 1948 / 10538.

Not validated: end-to-end TP > 1 (kernel level only shrinks N). Uneven EP splits (expert count not divisible by the EP size) are out of scope. `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` are clean on the changed files.

## Details

Design. `TrtLlmNvFp4LoRAExperts(TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsBase, _TrtLlmLoRAExpertsBase)`: the NVFP4 base comes first in the MRO, so `expects_unquantized_inputs` (per-token: the experts quantize the input themselves), `process_weights_after_loading` (`g1_scale_c`, folded clamp/beta) and the kernel arguments come from the existing NVFP4 experts. The `_TrtLlmLoRAExpertsBase` flow is unchanged: the gate/up delta is computed by punica on the unquantized input and passed as `gemm1_lora_delta`; the down delta is computed from the BF16 FC1 activation the kernel returns; the base finalize and the delta reduction run in one pass. Per-expert deltas already arrive as `[up | gate]`; fused 3D adapters are flipped from the checkpoint `[gate | up]` order.

Why per-token only. With static global input scales and `gemm1_lora_delta`, FlashInfer 0.7.2 returns the FC1 activation as `uint8` with `I / 2` columns, i.e. packed FP4 without block scales (observed on GB300). The down delta cannot be computed from it, the same situation as MXFP8 activations in #61979. With per-token scales the activation comes back as BF16 with `I` columns.

Limitations, each rejected rather than computed wrong:

- Gated SiLU only; other activations (`SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE`, `SITU`, non-gated) are not enabled for the LoRA class (untested).
- Llama4 routing (router weight applied on the input) is rejected: the LoRA finalize weights the output again.
- DP, all2all and EPLB are rejected, as for `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts`: the inherited no-LoRA fast path reads the local batch's adapter flag.
- `fully_sharded_loras` is rejected for all TRTLLM LoRA experts (BF16, MXFP4, NVFP4) through a new `FusedMoEConfig.is_lora_fully_sharded` / `_supports_fully_sharded_lora()` check: the shared flow computes the W13 delta with `add_inputs=False`, which the fully sharded punica path asserts against. With an explicit `flashinfer_trtllm` this raises at selection; BF16 `auto` falls back to Triton.
- With LoRA enabled, the NVFP4 and MXFP4 oracles try only the LoRA experts class, so the error names the unsupported feature (quantization scheme, routing) instead of the last candidate's generic reason.
- When the MoE layer has no LoRA context (adapters only on attention), the TRTLLM LoRA experts run the base path, like `TritonExperts`, instead of asserting.
- FlashInfer 0.7.2 has no tile-192 kernel for this dtype with the LoRA-delta epilogue, but advertises 192 as a candidate tile (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8272). The default tactic picks 192 once a launch averages more than 192 tokens per local expert, and autotuning tries it whenever it is a candidate, so an earlier head of this PR failed at warmup with the default `max_num_batched_tokens`. LoRA launches are therefore split to at most `192 * local_num_experts // top_k` tokens (the unfinalized outputs are concatenated, so the w2 delta and finalize are unchanged) and run outside FlashInfer autotuning, so the heuristic never reaches 192. No-LoRA launches are still autotuned. Both can go once FlashInfer ships the kernel or filters the tile.
- Launches above the TRTLLM NVFP4 launch limit (`_get_chunk_size()`) are split instead of raising.

Also fixed on the way, since this PR is the first fused-3D path whose intermediate gets padded at TP 1: `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA._slice_w13_b` returned early at TP 1 (and under EP, where the MoE TP size is 1), so a fused 3D `[gate | up]` adapter was copied unpadded into the padded buffer and the up half was misaligned. The early return is removed; `tests/lora/test_moe_lora_ep_load.py` covers TP 1 with padding. CI: `tests/lora/test_trtllm_nvfp4_lora_moe.py` and `tests/lora/test_trtllm_mxfp4_lora_moe.py` are added to the B200 kernels job.

Related work: #61979 (MXFP4 sibling, same structure); #34421 routes NVFP4 LoRA to Marlin.

+    scale = block_scale.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).double()

+def _lora_reference(reference, context, x, ids, weights, slots, offset, clamp):
+    w13, w2 = reference

+    s = torch.tensor(slots, device="cuda")
+    has = (s >= 0).double()[:, None]
+    s = s.clamp(min=0)
+    out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], K, dtype=torch.float64, device="cuda")
+    for k in range(TOPK):
+        local = ids[:, k].long() - offset
+        mask = ((local >= 0) & (local < num_local)).double()[:, None]
+        e = local.clamp(0, num_local - 1)
+        h = torch.einsum("tk,tnk->tn", xq, w13[e])
+        halves = []
+        for i, half in enumerate((h[:, :N], h[:, N:])):
+            a = context.w13_lora_a_stacked[i][s, e].double()
+            b = context.w13_lora_b_stacked[i][s, e].double()
+            delta = torch.einsum("tr,tnr->tn", torch.einsum("tk,trk->tr", xd, a), b)
+            halves.append(half + has * delta)
+        gate, up = halves
+        if clamp is not None:

+        act = (torch.nn.functional.silu(gate) * up).to(torch.bfloat16)

+        a2 = context.w2_lora_a_stacked[0][s, e].double()
+        b2 = context.w2_lora_b_stacked[0][s, e].double()
+        d2 = torch.einsum("tn,trn->tr", act.double(), a2)
+        d2 = torch.einsum("tr,tkr->tk", d2, b2)

No behavior change for the non-LoRA path. `_routed_moe_kwargs` only moves the existing kwargs out of `_invoke_kernel`; without LoRA the oracle tries the same kernel classes in the same order.

**Regression test**: `test_trtllm_fp4_moe_no_graph` now captures the call to `flashinfer.fused_moe.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` on the normal path and asserts the full kwarg set (names, tensor values, scalars) matches the previous explicit call, for all 7 activation cases x 3 shapes. On GB200 it passes on main and on this PR (23 passed, 2 skipped); dropping a single kwarg (`tune_max_num_tokens`) from the helper makes 19 cases fail.

**GSM8K** (`nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, GB200; a log line confirmed which experts class ran):

| config | experts class | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP2 + EP | `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsModular` | 0.871 / 0.884 (two runs) | 0.877 |
| TP1 | `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsMonolithic` | 0.882 | 0.884 |

The PR is within main's own run-to-run spread on the modular path, and throughput is the same (~8.2k output tok/s).
